text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said the government has decided to monitor all the economic indicators to ensure effective implementation of the 1997/98 (July-June) budget.

- Pakistan's software exports are expected to swell to $50 million by the end of the year following the exemptions of sales tax and customs duty on the import of computer equipments, mainly used in software development.
- At least 24 people were buried alive in a landslide caused by heavy rains, thunder and lightning in Mansehra district of the North West Frontier Province.
- Five people were killed and eight wounded in a grenade explosion in Karachi.
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan has lowered the value of the rupee by 0.07 against the U.S. dollar.
- Pakistan is seeking a concessional assistance of $100 million from the World Bank for poverty alleviation programme.

- Hyundai Engineering and Construction Co Ltd officials held discussions with Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif on the possibility of investment in Pakistan's infrastructure development in fields like communication, oil refinery and hydel power generation.
- A 12-month standby letter of credit from Water and Power Development Authority for the purchase of power from Hub Power Co was signed in Karachi on Saturday.
- Pakistani lawyers observed a strike across the country to protest killings of six lawyers in sectarian violence.
- Ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto has demanded formation of a national government in Pakistan comprising political parties, armed forces and state security agencies.
